correctness.rationale: From separability of the vertex subalgebra and radical-square-zero multiplication, normalized derivations form a direct sum of 2-by-2 matrix Lie algebras modulo graph-incidence vertex-scalar coboundaries. Every nonscalar 2-by-2 matrix has a 2-dimensional centralizer. In characteristic two the trace-pairing identity gives q^3-q traceless nonscalar X and q^2 solutions Y per prescribed nonzero scalar commutator, giving q^3(q^2-1); scalar zero fibers equal q^6+q^5-q^3 in all characteristics. Vertex-potential averaging and subset expansion prove the exact general formula, including parallel and isolated edges. Standalone verify.py exhaustively enumerated matrix fibers over q=2,3,4,5 and direct quotient commuting pairs for the documented small graph examples. Finite tests are not substituted for the proof.
